raw_plan.interpretation: I interpret “one acquisition email” as one membership-acquisition email for solution-aware TV shoppers comparing shortlisted OLED or Mini-LED models. Because the current dossier rates this audience DISCOVERY_ONLY, the email is a narrowly scoped proposition-validation message, not a recommendation to scale outreach or a claim that membership will select the right TV for the reader.

intent.desired_action: Join RTINGS membership to access its test results and product-comparison tools.

raw_plan.reader: A solution-aware OLED or Mini-LED shopper comparing shortlisted televisions against room, size, use-case, and budget constraints.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A TV shopper with a shortlist who needs to know which model fits their specific room, size, and use case
raw_plan.reader_scope: Qualified scope: individual or household OLED and Mini-LED buyers with a shortlist. Do not generalize the proposition to every TV shopper or imply knowledge of the recipient’s models, room, budget, purchase deadline, or prior research.
raw_plan.promise: RTINGS membership gives shortlisted OLED and Mini-LED buyers access to consistently measured test data and comparison tools they can use to examine consequential differences between models.
raw_plan.orientation: RTINGS is an independent testing and review site that gives TV shoppers standardized results and tools for comparing shortlisted models.
raw_plan.arc: A single-step validation argument: connect the reader’s shortlist decision to comparable underlying measurements, explain how RTINGS produces those measurements, then invite the reader to assess whether membership provides the evidence needed for the decision.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: With only one email, the argument must stand alone. It leads with the decision-relevant value of comparable underlying data rather than an unsupported pain story, uses the controlled testing process to make that value credible, and answers why membership offers more than a headline score. The join page is the documented acquisition destination, but the email must not imply that joining guarantees the right purchase. The dossier classifies this opportunity as DISCOVERY_ONLY, so response should validate the proposition before any broader outreach. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign: Which customers or quotes may we name?

emails.selection_reason: This proposition directly supports the selected reader’s shortlist decision with the strongest licensed mechanism: raw data measured consistently enough to compare products across brands and models. It gives the reader a concrete reason to consider membership without inventing a personal pain or promising a purchase outcome.
emails.target_audience: OLED and Mini-LED shoppers comparing shortlisted TVs for their room, size, use case, and budget.
emails.job: Earn a membership evaluation by showing how access to comparable underlying test data can inform a shortlisted-TV decision.
emails.single_idea: Membership lets a shopper look beyond summary scores to the underlying, consistently measured test data when comparing shortlisted TVs.
emails.felt_need: I need to determine which shortlisted TV best corresponds to my needs and budget.
emails.mechanism: RTINGS provides the raw data behind every score and says its controlled, repeatable lab process supports comparisons across brands, models, and years. Membership provides unlimited access to test results and product-comparison tools.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: This is a credible secondary acquisition bet for a high-consideration TV purchase: emphasize the provenance and inspectability of the testing rather than the granularity of comparison data.
alternative_arguments.single_idea: Membership provides access to results from products RTINGS buys itself, with published methods, photos, and videos available for scrutiny.
alternative_arguments.felt_need: I want evidence I can inspect before relying on a TV review for my shortlist.
alternative_arguments.mechanism: RTINGS buys products consumers can purchase and publishes its testing methods, photos, and videos so results can be verified and compared. Membership provides unlimited access to test results and comparison tools.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: a review score requires taking the publisher’s process largely on trust. After: RTINGS exposes both the tested-product provenance and supporting testing material for inspection.
must_not_say: Do not claim that the recipient distrusts reviews or has previously been misled.
Do not claim that self-purchased units eliminate all bias, regional variation, production changes, or unit-to-unit variation.
Do not claim named-customer adoption, testimonials, or proven purchase outcomes.
Do not describe RTINGS as the only review site with these practices or claim competitors cannot match them.
Do not mention membership prices, guarantees, or plan-specific terms.
alternative_arguments.objection: Why should I trust the testing behind the recommendation?
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether access to RTINGS’ testing evidence is useful enough to support the shortlisted-TV evaluation.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: Membership provides unlimited access to test results and product-comparison tools; RTINGS also publishes methods, photos, and videos for its results.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: Joining does not establish that a particular TV fits the reader’s room, budget, region, or preferences, and the supplied evidence does not enumerate every membership feature or plan difference.
alternative_arguments.subject_strategy: Earn attention with the inspectable provenance behind a TV score—products RTINGS buys and testing material readers can examine—without using unsupported exclusivity or trust claims.

emails.belief_shift: Before: the score is the main usable output of a TV review. After: the underlying data, measured through a repeatable process, can be inspected across shortlisted models.
must_not_say: Do not claim that membership will identify, choose, or guarantee the best TV for the reader.
Do not imply that every TV shopper, room, model, or regional variant is covered by this proposition.
Do not invent the recipient’s room conditions, shortlisted models, installed tools, past failures, urgency, or purchase deadline.

Do not describe the detailed behavior of the TV comparison, recommendation, results-table, custom-ratings, or size-to-distance tools; the licensed evidence establishes only their listing or availability.
Do not claim named-customer adoption, testimonials, conversion results, time savings, or better purchase outcomes.
Do not claim that RTINGS is uniquely capable, superior to named competitors, or the only service using standardized testing.
Do not cite the 558-TV count as current or attach a measurement date or methodology to it.
Do not mention membership prices, discounts, tax treatment, introductory duration, refund terms, guarantees, or unverified plan differences.
Do not broaden this validated scope beyond OLED and Mini-LED shortlist buyers.
Do not claim retailer specifications or overall scores are inaccurate or inherently inadequate.
emails.objection: Will membership provide anything useful beyond a headline score?
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether RTINGS membership provides enough comparative evidence to support the reader’s shortlisted-TV evaluation.
emails.next_step_value: Membership provides unlimited access to test results, product-comparison tools, and website features, including access to the raw data behind scores.
emails.next_step_limit: The join action does not determine which TV the reader should buy, guarantee fit for a specific room or use case, or establish the exact behavior and plan availability of every comparison feature.
emails.subject_strategy: Frame the open around what sits behind a TV score and why consistently measured underlying data matters when comparing a shortlist; avoid hype, unsupported outcomes, and generic membership language.
